explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is a Python client library (agentic-doc) that wraps the LandingAI Agentic Document Extraction REST API.  
   - Its goal is to let downstream Python code call a single parse(...) function (or specialized helpers) to extract structured data from PDFs/images/URLs, handle large‐file splitting, parallelism, retries, and offer utilities (visualizers, connectors).

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top-level files:  
     • pyproject.toml: build and dependency config  
     • .github/workflows/ci_cd.yml: CI/CD pipeline  
     • README.md, LICENSE, .flake8, .gitignore: docs and linting  
   - agentic_doc/ (the library source)  
     • common.py – core data models, error schemas  
     • config.py – environment/.env driven settings (batch size, retry caps, logging style)  
     • connectors.py – abstraction over document sources (Local, URL, S3, Google Drive)  
     • parse.py – main API surface: parse, parse_documents, parse_and_save…; splits large docs, thread pool orchestration, stitches results  
     • utils.py – visualization: bounding‐box snippets, debug images  
   - tests/ – unit & integration tests validating connectors, parse logic, utils, config, common.

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   - Emphasis on:  
     • Single-call API to parse local files, URLs, raw bytes  
     • Automatic PDF splitting + parallel processing + retry with backoff  
     • Connectors to abstract away different storage backends  
     • Utilities for saving groundings and visual debugging  

4. System design diagram guidance  
   a. Main components to represent:  
     1. Client Application (your Python code that does “from agentic_doc.parse import parse”)  
     2. agentic_doc Library (five sub-modules)  
        – API Layer (parse, parse_documents)  
        – Connector Layer (LocalConnector, S3Connector, GDriveConnector, URLConnector)  
        – Processing Layer (PDF splitter, thread‐pool executor, retry mechanism)  
        – Common/Data Model Layer (Pydantic schemas, chunk & grounding models)  
        – Utility Layer (viz_parsed_document, save groundings)  
     3. External Dependencies  
        – LandingAI Agentic Document Extraction REST API  
        – OpenCV (cv2) for image reading  
        – AWS/GCP if using S3/GDrive connectors  
     4. Configuration / Env Var Store (.env, os.environ)  

   b. Relationships & interactions (data flow):  
     1. Client → calls parse()  
     2. parse() reads Settings from config.py (env or .env)  
     3. parse() uses Connector(s) to fetch raw bytes / file paths / URLs  
     4. Processing Layer splits large PDFs (if needed)  
     5. Thread‐pool: workers perform HTTP calls with retry/backoff → AgenticDoc API  
     6. Responses aggregated, stitched into hierarchical JSON (common.py models)  
     7. Results returned to Client  
     8. Optional: utils.viz_parsed_document → produce annotated images  

   c. Architectural patterns & principles:  
     - Layered architecture: API, Connectors, Processing, Utilities  
     - Strategy pattern for connectors  
     - Builder/Data Mapper for Pydantic models (common.py)  
     - Concurrency via thread pool + batching  
     - Resilience: retry with exponential backoff, jitter  

   d. Key technologies & libraries:  
     - Python 3.9+  
     - requests or httpx (for REST calls)  
     - concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor  
     - Pydantic (for result schemas)  
     - OpenCV-Python (cv2)  
     - AWS SDK (boto3) / Google API Client  
     - dotenv (for .env support)  

5. Tailoring the diagram for this library project  
   - Focus on core parsing pipeline and extensibility via connectors.  
   - Emphasize that connectors are plug-ins that produce a uniform input (bytes or path).  
   - Show splitting/stitching logic as a sub-pipeline within Processing Layer.  
   - Highlight error‐handling/retry loop around each HTTP call.  
   - Show utils as side branch off main pipeline for optional visualization.

6. Diagram elements to include  
   - Clear labels on each component box (e.g., “parse() API Layer”, “LocalConnector”)  
   - Directional arrows showing flow (Client → API Layer → Connectors → Processing → External API → back)  
   - Color coding or shapes:  
     • Blue boxes for internal modules (agentic_doc/*)  
     • Green cylinders for external systems (REST API, S3, GDrive)  
     • Yellow box for Client Application  
     • Annotate thread pool & retry as special icons or styling.  

7. Detail emphasis  
   - Ensure you capture all five internal modules and how they interconnect.  
   - Show configuration as a separate “Settings” box feeding into API Layer and Processing Layer.  
   - Mark parallelism (BATCH_SIZE × MAX_WORKERS) near the thread‐pool icon.  
   - Don’t omit the connectors’ strategy extension points—they’re key to library extensibility.

By following these guidelines, your system design diagram will accurately reflect the agentic-doc library’s architecture, illustrating data flow, module boundaries, and external dependencies in a clear, maintainable way.  
</explanation>
